ai.description: This slender snake reaches 1 meter. It is olive-brown with a distinct pale-banded snout and a horizontal pupil. It is identified by its blunt, rounded head and lack of a prominent rostral appendage.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ahaetulla fronticincta* is uniquely identified by its distinctly blunt, rounded snout, which contrasts with the sharply pointed or elongated rostral appendages of other Indian *Ahaetulla* species.
ai.habitat: The River Vine Snake inhabits dense riparian vegetation and mangrove forests, typically found at low elevations near freshwater or brackish water bodies in the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: The River Vine Snake is primarily diurnal and specializes in hunting fish, frequently positioning itself along branches overhanging water to strike at aquatic prey.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ahaetulla fronticincta* is ovoviviparous, producing litters of 3–9 young. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ahaetulla fronticincta* is found in the lowlands of Northeast India (Assam and West Bengal) and Bangladesh, typically inhabiting riparian and mangrove environments.
